question: Do the presently available Jordan and Spin(2,3) representation data force the physical aggregate intertwiner to have multiplicity one or force all Schur packets onto one projective ray?

inputBoundary.physicalCensus: Claim 1512: each fixed Pati-Salam bidoublet carrier has gauge Clebsch multiplicity one, but the published carrier is generation blind and leaves End(C^3). The bounded masked minimal tree census has one packet only by absence.
inputBoundary.jordanCarrier: Claims 1109 and 1126-1127: each local relation wheel is H_2(R)/Spin(2,3); two untyped overlapping wheels generate H_3(R)/Sp(6,R); opposite-anchor typing prevents that mixed closure.
inputBoundary.nullCone: Claim 1513: three nonaligned packets can lie on a complex or real-indefinite quadratic null cone, but cone invariance does not force nullness.

factorizationTheorem.statement: If an algebra or group A acts on U and U' but trivially on family multiplicity F, then Hom_A(U tensor F,U' tensor F) is Hom_A(U,U') tensor End(F).
factorizationTheorem.consequence: Adding a Jordan/Spin(2,3) action on an external response factor, while it remains trivial on F, cannot turn the sourced Pati-Salam gauge intertwiner into a unique physical family intertwiner.

familyCentralizerLadder.meaning: C direct-sum M_2(C); choosing the selected line still leaves unrestricted complement rotations

familyCentralizerLadder.data: one local P-I Jordan wheel with N spectator
familyCentralizerLadder.meaning: one scalar on the connected P-I block and one on N

familyCentralizerLadder.data: both untyped overlapping P-I and P-N wheels
familyCentralizerLadder.meaning: multiplicity one is reached, but the mixed Jordan product generates X_IN and the closure is H_3(R)/Sp(6,R), not the protected pair of local Spin(2,3) wheels

typedAnchorTheorem.model: Two independently typed irreducible H_2 relation sectors on C^2_D direct-sum C^2_M, with sector projectors retained so cross-sector composition is forbidden.
typedAnchorTheorem.centralizer: C on the Dirac wheel direct-sum C on the Majorana wheel
typedAnchorTheorem.consequence: Opposite-anchor typing protects the null mask but does not equate the two sector normalizations. A cross-anchor sewing law is needed to reduce the two scalars to one common scalar.
typedAnchorTheorem.unsafeAlternative: Forgetting the type projectors and joining the two relations on one P/I/N carrier reduces the commutant to C only by restoring the mixed I-N relation and the Sp(6) envelope.

rankMismatchNoGo.statement: No invertible raw-family exchange can conjugate the rank-one selected projector P to the rank-two complement projector Q.
rankMismatchNoGo.proof: Similarity preserves trace and rank, but tr(P)=rank(P)=1 whereas tr(Q)=rank(Q)=2.
rankMismatchNoGo.consequence: The exchange real structure of the two-face H_2 carrier cannot act directly on the physical 1+2 family split; it must live on equal-dimensional scalar copies, a stabilized module, or a response carrier.

threePacketNullVectorTest.conditionalRepresentation: If the three packet minors are explicitly identified with the standard vector representation of SO(1,2), their quadratic form is the claim-1513 null form.
threePacketNullVectorTest.unbrokenSymmetryConsequence: A fixed coupling vector invariant under the full connected SO(1,2) must vanish, which returns all minors to zero and hence the common ray.
threePacketNullVectorTest.brokenOrbitConsequence: A nonzero null vector such as (5,4,3) lies on a symmetry-preserved orbit but is not itself invariant. Using it requires a null spurion or vacuum and breaks to its stabilizer.
threePacketNullVectorTest.currentStatus: The corpus contains no physical equivariant map from the aggregate packet-minor space to this Lorentz vector representation and no action or orbit constraint forcing a null vacuum.

aggregateVerdict.minimalMaskedTree: Multiplicity-one alignment is unnecessary because claim 1512 has only one retained packet; this is an absence theorem, not a representation theorem.
aggregateVerdict.publishedPhysicalCarrier: No multiplicity-one theorem: the exact relevant Hom space retains complex dimension 9.
aggregateVerdict.localJordanRepair: Insufficient: one wheel leaves centralizer dimension 2, while typed two-wheel separation leaves two sector scalars.
aggregateVerdict.untypedGlobalRepair: Achieves scalar commutant only at the cost of H_3(R)/Sp(6,R) closure and the mixed relation the mask was designed to exclude.
aggregateVerdict.nullConeRepair: Conditional only: full unbroken SO(1,2) would force zero minors, while a nonzero null orbit requires new spurion/dynamical data.

exactReopeningDatum.primary: A represented cross-anchor sewing morphism or natural transformation that identifies the Dirac-wheel and Majorana-wheel scalar intertwiners while keeping the mixed I-N composite in junk or outside the composable Hom set.
exactReopeningDatum.requiredCertificate: On the complete physical real-even Pati-Salam module, compute dim Hom_rel(aggregate source,aggregate target)=1, show all admitted packet columns factor through its generator, and verify that X_PI circle X_PN does not become a physical primitive I-N arrow.
exactReopeningDatum.nullOrbitAlternative: Provide an explicit equivariant identification of the three physical packet minors with an SO(1,2) vector plus a sourced invariant constraint or potential whose admissible vacuum forces q=0; state whether the vacuum is zero/common-ray or nonzero/symmetry-breaking.
exactReopeningDatum.falsifier: Two independent typed sector scalars, two independent physical Hom generators, or one surviving mixed I-N primitive arrow.

verdict: The available Jordan/Spin(2,3) data do not force aggregate multiplicity one. The only current finite-matrix route to a scalar commutant joins both wheels into the already-excluded H_3(R)/Sp(6,R) envelope; the protected typed construction retains a two-scalar ambiguity.
